stem: After completing a telehealth encounter, which documentation practice is appropriate?

options.A: Document the clinical encounter in the health record and identify that the encounter was conducted by telehealth
options.B: Document only the billing code because clinical notes are unnecessary for a virtual encounter
options.C: Omit the encounter from the health record unless the client specifically asks for documentation
options.D: Use less complete clinical documentation than would be required for comparable in-person care

rationale: HHS telehealth workflow guidance directs clinicians to document that an encounter was a telehealth visit, and federal documentation guidance continues to require complete clinical documentation of patient encounters. Therefore A is correct. A virtual modality does not remove the need for a clinical record, and documentation is not optional based on patient request.
educational_objective: Document telehealth encounters as clinical encounters in the health record and identify the telehealth modality of care without reducing documentation completeness.
source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services — Telehealth.HHS.gov
source_locator: Follow up after telehealth visits — Documentation: document that this was a telehealth visit; use telehealth-specific billing codes/modifiers as applicable; workflow includes documentation as a core process
source_claim_supported: A telehealth encounter should be documented in the clinical record and identified as a telehealth visit; telehealth does not eliminate clinical documentation requirements.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Information Technology, printed p.22 / PDF p.26: enter computer documentation accurately, completely and in a timely manner
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Information Technology / telehealth documentation
correction_summary: Replaced a broad private-standard claim about mandatory telehealth-specific documentation elements with current HHS guidance. Retained the clinically relevant requirements to document the encounter and identify it as telehealth, while avoiding state- or payer-specific fields as universal rules.
audit_findings: A is directly supported by HHS workflow guidance and aligns with NCSBN documentation expectations. B, C and D incorrectly diminish clinical documentation requirements. No state-specific consent or payer-specific field is presented as a universal requirement, eliminating scope ambiguity.
audit_reviewer: GPT-5.6 Sol Rule 1 — item-by-item semantic audit
final_reaudit_scope: current HHS telehealth workflow guidance; A-D audit; avoidance of state/payer overgeneralization; NCSBN 2026 blueprint; independent adversarial second pass
